newsitem.title: USA: CME hogs and pork bellies seen steady to higher.
newsitem.headline: CME hogs and pork bellies seen steady to higher.

text.p: CME hog futures were expected to open steady to 0.100 cent per lb higher while pork bellies were called steady to 0.200 higher, livestock analysts said.

Carryover demand is seen after Wednesday's rally to net gains late in most nearby months, with mostly steady cash hog calls and higher pork cutout values also seen supportive. Cash loin prices were also expected to strengthen soon on anticipated retailer featuring over the Independence Day holiday, they said.
However, some analysts voiced caution as wet weather moving into the Midwest may increase hog movement and weigh on cash prices.

Pork belly futures also staged a rally late in the session Wednesday after dropping to limit losses, and most analysts look for carryover technical demand at the start. The stronger close after a limit loss looks technically strong on the charts. Higher cash belly prices and indications of a bullish USDA Cold Storage report Friday were also cited for demand, they said.

Analyst estimates on the Cold Storage report for frozen pork bellies in U.S. warehouses as of May 31 ranged from 53.7 million to 57.7 million lbs. This compares with 63.5 million lbs on hand last year and the record low for the period of 54.98 million lbs set in 1973.
